title: Light can break a bond
caption: A photon breaks a bond if its energy at least equals the bond energy. Cl–Cl is 242 kJ mol⁻¹, so wavelengths of 494 nm or shorter can split Cl₂ into radicals, which is why chlorination of methane starts in sunlight.
alt: Energy diagram: Cl₂ at the bottom, 2Cl• 242 kJ mol⁻¹ above, with a photon arrow of 494 nm reaching it.
description: Upper level: two chlorine radicals, 242 kJ mol⁻¹ higher.
A 494 nm photon carries exactly 242 kJ mol⁻¹.
